book.title: The Penguin Book of Independent Crosswords, volume 1

clue.text: What's the point of interrogating?

parts.note: the point is the punctuation dot placed at the end of a written question, not the purpose of questioning

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud whether questioning a suspect is worth the bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Point' reads as 'purpose', but it is a printed dot: the symbol ending every query has a dot at its foot.
explanation.definitionFit: The punctuation symbol written after a query is literally the dot that interrogative sentences end with.

clue.text: Cut up after drawing?

parts.note: recalls the old punishment of being hanged, drawn and then cut into four pieces

explanation.surface: An artist's sketch gets sliced to pieces once it is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing' suggests sketching, but the reference is the traitor's sentence 'hanged, drawn and quartered', where the body was cut into four after being drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: To divide into four parts is the last stage of the historic execution for treason, following the drawing.

clue.text: Ornamental stand set up before entrance

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word for entrance is written from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a gate is an entrance
ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: A decorative display stand is put up just ahead of the doorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set up' turns GATE into ETAG, which comes ahead of ERE.
explanation.definitionFit: An étagère is a piece of furniture with open shelves for displaying ornaments, a whatnot.

clue.text: Finance officer more confident after fixing of rate

indicators.note: the word for more confident comes after the rearranged letters
fixing suggests altering or rigging, so the letters of rate are rearranged

parts.note: surer means more certain, more confident

explanation.surface: A finance officer grows bolder once the interest rate has been fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixing of rate' sounds like a bank setting interest, which suits a finance officer, but 'fixing of' is the signal to rearrange; 'after' puts the comparative at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasurer manages the funds of a club, company or society, so is its financial official.

clue.text: Sea-ear is yellow floating on sea at St Malo

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first piece sits above, floating on top of, the second

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold or yellow
mer is French for sea, and St Malo is a French port

explanation.surface: A shellfish is described as a yellow thing bobbing on the waters off a French port.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is gold in heraldry; St Malo signals French, where sea is MER.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an edible abalone of the Channel Islands, also called the sea-ear for its ear-shaped shell.

clue.text: Man heard coming to the front brings us letters

indicators.note: coming to the front reads as the soundalike word going ahead of the word for front
heard means the word for man is taken by its sound, giving a soundalike spelling

parts.note: a man is a male
the van is the front of an army or procession

explanation.surface: A man everyone hears about arrives at the front with our post.
explanation.walkthrough: MALE said aloud gives MAIL; VAN is the front, as in vanguard.
explanation.definitionFit: A Post Office vehicle carries the post round, so it is what delivers our correspondence.

clue.text: Gentleman upset a German providing Italian dish

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word for gentleman is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: sir is the title or address of a gentleman
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A gentleman is put out because a German has served him an Italian meal.
explanation.walkthrough: SIR read upwards is RIS, and OTTO stands for any German.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is a rice dish cooked slowly in stock, a staple of northern Italian cooking.

clue.text: He is not a rude mongrel — if this

definitions.text: He is not a rude mongrel — if this

indicators.note: a mongrel is of mixed breed, so the preceding letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A dog of mixed breed will not misbehave indoors provided it has been trained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mongrel' mixes HE IS NOT A RUDE, and the whole clue describes the result: a dog that has learned not to foul the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A house-trained pet has been taught clean habits indoors, so it would not be a rude dog.

clue.text: Cow, one no longer alive on account of salt

parts.note: an ox is a bovine animal, loosely a cow
a means one
late means recently dead

explanation.surface: A cow and a dead beast are linked to some salt, as if killed by it.
explanation.definitionFit: An oxalate is a chemical salt of oxalic acid, found for instance in rhubarb leaves.

clue.text: Me? I love the gal and that's an understatement

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O
sis, short for sister, is an informal word for a girl

explanation.surface: Someone asks 'Me? I love the girl?' as if saying so were putting it mildly.
explanation.definitionFit: Meiosis is the rhetorical figure of deliberate understatement, making something seem smaller than it is.

clue.text: Immoral lady could make one err with sweet talk

indicators.note: the listed letters could be made into one new word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fallen woman's flattery might lead a man astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could make one' rearranges ERR plus SWEET TALK.
explanation.definitionFit: A streetwalker is a prostitute who solicits on the street, an old-fashioned euphemism for a loose woman.

clue.text: The folk providing your daily challenge can be dogs!

definitions.text: The folk providing your daily challenge
definitions.meaning: first meaning: crossword compilers, who supply a puzzle each day
second meaning: a breed of gundog, such as the Irish or English kind

explanation.surface: The people behind the daily crossword are cheekily called dogs.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark hints at an insult, but it is simply a second sense: the gundog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword compilers are called by this name, and it is also a family of pointing gundogs with long silky coats.

clue.text: Machine, one to 23

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tool or machine that drives rivets
second meaning: one who rivets, rivet being a synonym of the answer to 23, enthral

explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is ENTHRAL; to rivet someone is to enthral them, so one who does it is a riveter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a mechanical tool for fixing rivets and, figuratively, someone who holds an audience spellbound.

clue.text: Island one's found in family record

indicators.note: found in means one piece is located within the other

parts.note: a family tree records a family's descent
one is the Roman numeral I; the 's is read as 'is'

explanation.surface: An island turns up in somebody's family history.
explanation.walkthrough: Tiree is a small island of the Inner Hebrides, off the west coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiree is one of the Scottish Hebridean islands, known for its windswept beaches.

clue.text: Facial feature makes girl appear awfully morose on the outside

indicators.note: the jumbled letters of morose sit on the outside, around the girl
awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters of morose are rearranged

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl's prominent feature makes her look terribly gloomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Girl' and 'appear morose' suggest her expression, but the gloomy word is only letters, jumbled by 'awfully' and wrapped round her name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman nose is one with a high prominent bridge, like those on ancient Roman statues.

clue.text: Delivery boy in a muddle, terribly green

parts.note: a mess is a muddle

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so the letters of green are rearranged

explanation.surface: A young courier is hopelessly confused and very inexperienced.
explanation.walkthrough: MESS is followed by GREEN rearranged into ENGER by 'terribly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A messenger carries messages or parcels, a job traditionally done by an errand boy.

clue.text: Substance from whales or bears — grim, horrible

indicators.note: horrible suggests something mangled, so the letters of bears grim are rearranged

explanation.surface: A list of unpleasant products from whales or grim bears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Horrible' rearranges BEARS GRIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambergris is a waxy secretion from the intestines of sperm whales, prized in perfume-making.

clue.text: Our railway system's getting worse off, one reads

parts.note: BR is short for British Rail, the former UK national railway

indicators.note: off suggests something gone wrong, so the letters of worse are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grumble that Britain's railways keep deteriorating, as one reads in the papers.
explanation.walkthrough: BR is British Rail, once the national railway of the UK; 'off' rearranges WORSE into OWSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A browser looks casually through books or magazines, someone who dips into reading matter.

clue.text: Get knowledge back in Religious Education and Latin (merit)

parts.note: RE is the school subject abbreviation
to earn something is to merit it

explanation.surface: A pupil recovers knowledge in RE and Latin classes and gets a merit.
explanation.walkthrough: RE is Religious Education, a subject in British schools.
explanation.definitionFit: To relearn is to acquire again what you once knew and have forgotten.

clue.text: What we bend in the bar the Spanish bend too

definitions.text: What we bend in the bar

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
to bow is to bend

explanation.surface: In the pub we bend something, and Spaniards do the same.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bending the elbow' is an idiom for drinking, hence the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising a glass means flexing the arm joint, so drinking is jokingly called bending this joint.

clue.text: Embark on canal with food supply

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to ... a task is to begin it
second meaning: the alimentary canal, through which food passes

explanation.surface: Someone sets off along a waterway carrying provisions.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one word, the answer is a zoological term for the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: The enteron is the alimentary canal or gut cavity, while the two-word phrase means to begin something.

clue.text: Boy, tiny kid, ran amok inside

indicators.note: inside means the jumbled letters go within the other word

parts.note: a baby is a tiny child

indicators.note: running amok is wild and disordered, so the letters of ran are rearranged

explanation.surface: A little boy, still a toddler, charges wildly round indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boy' is the definition, a name rather than a lad; 'tiny kid' supplies the outer word and 'amok' jumbles the short verb set inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby is a male first name, as in Dickens's Barnaby Rudge.

clue.text: Blockheads — the North has lots

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for north
oodles means lots

explanation.surface: A jibe that northerners have plenty of fools.
explanation.definitionFit: A noodle is an informal word for a silly or stupid person, so the plural means dimwits.

clue.text: Tis to become alert

parts.note: in a down clue the word sit written upwards gives these letters

explanation.surface: An archaic 'tis' is offered as a call to wake up and pay attention.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue words are the result: SIT read 'up' a down entry spells TIS.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit up is to straighten and pay attention, an idiom for suddenly taking notice.

clue.text: Make a slave's entrance

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to enslave someone, the original sense
second meaning: as a verb, to put into a trance, captivate

explanation.surface: A slave makes a grand entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrance' looks like a noun, a way in, but it is the verb en-TRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word originally meant to hold in bondage, and now chiefly to captivate or spellbind.

clue.text: Desmond is unable to make music

parts.note: Des is short for Desmond
can't means cannot, is unable

explanation.surface: Poor Desmond has no musical ability.
explanation.definitionFit: To descant is to sing or play a melody above the main tune, so it is a way of performing.

clue.text: Rubbish bag initially stored in building by house?

indicators.note: stored in means one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: a garage is a building beside a house

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of bag

explanation.surface: A sack of rubbish is first kept in the outbuilding next to the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Garbage is refuse or waste, the American word for household trash.

clue.text: A photograph's obviousness

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a slide, a photograph on film viewed by light shone through it
second meaning: the quality of being easily seen through

explanation.surface: A snapshot's plainness.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a photographic slide and also the quality of being clear or easily detected.
